codkit PROP-016: Project types
1. Purpose and vocabulary

The engine of Codkit - patch sets, grafts, the own layer, the drift guard, `load`/`save`/`sync`, the generated branch, `cycle`, `rebase-onto-pin`, `publish`, licensing, standards delivery, the agent protocol - is universal. What is not universal is the knowledge of one family of upstreams: where own code lives, which file is the product manifest, how a service is overridden, how the tree is built and tested, which icons a distribution carries. Until now that knowledge sat inline in the engine and was VS Code's. A **project type** carries it instead, so that the same tool serves several VS Code forks, several Theia forks, and later products that are not IDEs. @status:spec/plan

A **project type** (short: type) is the tool's knowledge of one family of upstreams, shipped as one package and named by one identifier: `vscode`, `generic`, `theia`, later others. A patch set declares exactly one type. The engine asks the type; it never states a type's facts itself. @status:spec/done

A **capability** is a named optional ability a type declares (`brand-images`, `gen-brand`, `build-channels`, `runtime-library`, `own-extensions`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `dev-channel`, `upgrade-advisory`). A verb that needs a capability refuses when the type does not declare it (`TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`). @status:spec/done

A **type package** is the npm package that implements a type against the contract package `@codkit/type-api`: `@codkit/type-vscode`, `@codkit/type-generic`, `@codkit/type-theia`. The tool repository is an npm workspace holding the CLI package and the official type packages side by side; each is published on its own at the development version 1.0.0 (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0`). @status:spec/done
2. The contract: ten questions a type answers

The contract is exactly the list of variation points measured in the engine (DESIGN-001 §1); a question is added to it only when a second type needs it, never in anticipation. Each area below is one object of small functions on the `ProjectType` interface of `@codkit/type-api`. The tenth area, generators, was added on 2026-09-09 exactly so: the second type needs a different skeleton (an inversify container module instead of a workbench contribution) and has no string-funnel graft at all. @status:spec/done

**Upstream identity.** The tag pattern a pin may use, how a pin resolves to `tag@sha@date` (universal form), the fingerprints `check-tree` requires of a healthy tree (manifest name, marker files), the anchor policy. @status:spec/done

**Tree layout.** The own root (`typeConfig.ownRoot`, a path from the tree root: `src/vs/<name>` for VS Code, a workspace package for Theia), whether own extensions exist and where they materialize, the cleanup whitelist of build outputs the fresh pass may remove, the forbidden patch targets, type-specific marker comment forms if any. **Amended 2026-09-09 after the second real type:** a type may name **several owned directories** (`ownRoots`: the own root plus, for a family whose application is a directory of the product, the application root), each mirrored by content, excluded from the drift guard and named in the inventory like the own root; and it names the **build outputs inside an owned directory** (`ownBuildOutputs`, globs relative to the owned root, e.g. `lib/**`, `*.tsbuildinfo`) that the mirror never copies to the delta, `status` never counts as changed own code, and the fresh pass may remove - because a family that compiles a package in place writes its output next to its sources. @status:spec/done

**Layers.** `own`, `patch`, `resource-file` and `rewrite-rule` are universal and always present. `config-overlay` takes its targets and its optional dev channel from the type (VS Code: `product.json` with `product.overrides.json`). `own-extension` takes its materializer from the type (VS Code: `extensions/<name>`). `service-override` takes its verifier from the type (VS Code: `registerSingleton`; Theia: an inversify `rebind` in a container module). `entry-module` takes its locator from the type (VS Code: `workbench.common.main.ts`; Theia: the application's module list). A layer the type does not provide is absent for that patch set: `verify` refuses an artifact of that layer with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`. @status:spec/done

**Build and test.** The dependency install, the **dependency roots** (##TYPE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS), the hygiene and lint scripts, the compile channels behind `build up|down|status|errors` and the foreign-watcher markers, the test runner with an own-root glob, the package build, the product's own packaging step, the stamps the packaging needs and where its artifacts land (##TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS). `ci --profile build` is one universal skeleton (PROP-011) whose steps call these answers, and `codkit package` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE`) is the run that reaches the distributable. @status:spec/done

**Packaging is five answers of the area, and all of them are common fields of the contract** - the engine runs what it is handed and never learns whose packager it is. `packageBuild` is the family's build of the application. `packageDistributable` is the product's own step after it - an installer, an archive, a signed bundle - and is a **separate** list precisely because the two have different authors: `codkit package --skip-type-build` runs only the second half over a tree the watch channels already built, and a family or a patch set with no such step answers with an empty list. `packageStamps` are the environment variables the packaging needs, each with the value that fills it - a value of the run (`tree-head`, `pin-tag`, `pin-date`) or the type's own word (`literal`, whose value comes from the type's own configuration); a family that bakes nothing at build time answers with none, and what an operator already exported is never overwritten (##TYPE-STAMPS-FILL-A-GAP). `packageOutputs` are **path patterns from the tree root** naming where the artifacts land, matched segment by segment with `*` never crossing a `/` and a trailing `/` meaning a directory; a pattern that would leave the tree is refused, so a family whose packager writes **beside** the managed tree answers with an empty list and says so rather than pointing the engine at a directory the tool neither manages nor guards (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#VSCODE-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS`). Measured on 2026-09-09 by the first product that had to reach a distributable: until then `packageBuild` was a field of the contract that no module of the engine read. @status:spec/done

A family with several distributable targets answers a closed `packageTargets` catalog: stable id, platform, architecture, build commands and the host operating systems on which those commands run natively (`supportedHosts`). Four answers of a target are optional, added on 2026-09-24 with the Linux installers of the first family: `outputs`, the tree-relative patterns of its artifacts (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-TARGET-OUTPUTS`); `container`, the route of the hosts it names - `hosts`, `recipe` (the absolute path of a directory of the type package holding a `Dockerfile`), `treeArguments` (a build argument read from a file of the tree), `buildEnvironment` and `runEnvironment` (the names, or `prefix*` patterns, of the variables of codkit's environment that the image build and the container receive) (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER`); `hostRefusal`, the reason and the hint of the refusal on a host with no route (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-HOST-ROUTES`); and `inputs(treeDir)`, what its build downloads - `{name, from, path, use}`, `use` being one of `environment`, `fetch`, `directory` and `tree` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS`). `defaultPackageTargets` is the patch-set-selected bare-command list. The engine may select an exact id, one platform family, or `all`, but never accepts a command string from project configuration. `all` means every catalog target with a route on the current host - native or container; it is not a claim that installers, signing or native modules are universally cross-compilable. A target build command may resolve target-owned environment such as a Windows SDK tool before spawn; a missing tool refuses as package environment failure. `projectTypeProblems` holds the new answers to their shape: a container names at least one host and none of the `supportedHosts`, its recipe is an absolute path, and an output pattern stays inside the tree. @status:impl/done

**A packager edits the tree while it packages, and the paths it edits are the type's fifth packaging answer** (`packageScratch`, the same patterns as `packageOutputs`). They are not artifacts: they are tracked files of the upstream that the packaging rewrote in passing - a manifest whose version it bumps, a flag it flips from a development build to a production one - and after a successful run they are what makes an otherwise clean tree dirty. `codkit package` therefore returns exactly these paths to the tip of the loaded tree when the packaging is over, in the same `finally` as the overlay restore and before it, and it returns them whatever the verdict of the packaging and **even under `--keep-overlay`**: that flag was asked to keep the materialization for a hand check of the package, and nobody ever asked for the residue. Only tracked paths that actually changed are touched and reported (`data.scratchRestored`); an untracked file is left where it is, because removing one is what `load --fresh` does and never a side effect of packaging. `codkit status` reads the same answer: a changed upstream file matching these patterns is named as packaging residue in `data.upstream.packagingScratch`, and while such files are all a tree carries the advice is `codkit load --fresh --discard` and not `save` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#STATUS-ADVICE-FOLLOWS-THE-LAYER`). Measured on 2026-09-09: the first successful `codkit package` of a real fork left one rewritten manifest behind and `status` advised extracting a build side effect into the delta. @status:impl/done

**A stamp of a type fills a gap in the environment; it never argues with the operator.** `codkit package` resolves each name of `build.packageStamps` against the environment it was started in: a name that already carries a non-empty value keeps that value and is printed as `stamp <name>=<value> (from environment)`, and only an absent or empty name is filled from the type's answer. The reason is what the stamps are for: a family declares them because its packager reads a variable nobody remembers to set (a commit, a channel, a date), not because the tool has an opinion about a variable somebody set deliberately - and the run that measured this had to be told a channel the type could not yet name, found the type's value written over its own, and could not package at all. An exported name with an empty value is an empty value and not an answer, so the type still fills it. The names that came from the environment travel in `--json` as `data.stampsFromEnvironment` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE`). Measured on 2026-09-09 on the first real distributable of the first family. @status:impl/done

**Which compile channels a run that names none starts is the type's answer** (`build.defaultChannels`), not a constant of the engine. `codkit build up` without `--channel` and the single pass of `ci --profile build` both took the pair `['transpile', 'typecheck']` from a module of the watch wrapper - the channel names of the first family - and the second family, whose channels are `typecheck` and `bundle`, therefore had a build profile that type-checked and **never bundled its application**, while calling itself the build profile. The answer is a list of names: the profile's own names are what it selects from, a name the profile does not declare is ignored, and a type that names none has every declared channel as its default, so the bare form of a command is never a refusal over a name from another family. `vscode` answers `transpile, typecheck`; `theia` answers `typecheck, bundle`; `generic` answers every channel the patch set declared, in the order it declared them. The word `transpile` joined the dictionary of the blindness gate in the same change (##TYPE-ENGINE-IS-BLIND), so the next constant of this shape cannot reach the engine quietly. @status:impl/done

**Upgrade advisory.** The semantic readers the cycle runs between two pins (VS Code: built-in extensions of `product.json`, Electron and TypeScript versions). The advisory's frame - what changed, what it means, what to do - is the engine's. @status:spec/done
**Brand images** (capability `brand-images`). The target table of the distribution's icons and image forms; the generator, the index and the verifier are the engine's. @status:spec/done
**Runtime library** (capability `runtime-library`). Which shipped runtime package the type delivers with `codkit runtime load` (today's library becomes `runtime-vscode`). @status:spec/done

**Standards and skills.** The standard `minimal-intervention` is universal; the seam catalogue and the list "how upstream would build it" that `ck-intervene` routes through come from the type's packages (`seams-vscode`). @status:spec/done

**Conventions.** The subsystems of intervention ids, the forbidden service ids, the defaults of `conventions.json` a product may extend through `conventionsExtensionFile`; the marker grammar and the id pattern's shape stay the engine's. @status:spec/done

**Generators.** The skeletons `gen feature` writes (the feature class, its flag declaration, its test) and the string-funnel graft `gen brand` prints are the type's: for VS Code a workbench contribution with DI and the `nls.ts` hook, for Theia an inversify container module with a preference-backed flag and no funnel graft (capability `gen-brand` absent). The engine owns the command, the header handling (`GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`), the refusal over existing files and the test location rule; the type supplies the templates and the reminders. @status:spec/done

**Which directories hold the installed dependencies is the type's answer, not the engine's.** The build profile refuses over a tree whose dependencies never arrived, and `publish` carries them into its disposable fork; both used a module constant of the engine, `['node_modules', 'build/node_modules']` - the two install roots of the first family, which reached the engine before there was a contract to put them in. A second family has one root and no `build/` directory at all, so the constant made `ci --profile build` unable to go green over any tree of it, and said so with a message asking for a directory the tree already had. The contract therefore carries `build.dependencyRoots`, a list of tree-relative directories; the engine asks for the npm receipt `<root>/.package-lock.json` inside each of them (an empty bind mount is not a restored cache, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#CI-DEPS-POLICY-M1`) and **names the receipts that are missing** rather than the first root of a list it made up. Measured by the first real consumer of the second type. @status:impl/done

**Where an input may land is bounded by answers the type already gives; there is no question of its own.** The engine refuses a `to` that meets (PROP-007 `INPUTS-PLACEMENT`): an owned directory of `layout.ownRoots`; the materialization directory of `layout.ownExtensionPath`; a directory of `build.dependencyRoots`; a pattern of `layout.cleanupWhitelist`; `build.packageOutputs` and the `outputs` of `build.packageTargets`. No area was added for it (`##TYPE-CONTRACT-IS-CLOSED`): these answers already name every place the machinery of a family writes into, and the other owners of a path - the pin and the patch set - are the engine's to read. The three official types answer them already - `vscode` with its own root, `extensions/`, its two dependency roots, its cleanup whitelist and its package outputs; `theia` with its owned directories - the own root and the application - its dependency root, its cleanup whitelist and the package outputs of its application; `generic` with its own root, its dependency root and the cleanup whitelist of its configuration - so an input is placed by one rule under every type. @status:impl/done

**A type whose answers are a function of its own configuration.** Most types answer the same thing for every patch set and state their areas as constants. A type of a family with no product model cannot: which JSON files an overlay may target, what installs and tests the tree, whether there are compile channels at all is knowledge only the patch set has (`TYPE-GENERIC`). Such a type answers one more member of the interface, `configure(typeConfig)`, and the engine calls it exactly once - after `configSchema` has accepted the section and before any engine is asked anything - and hands the RESULT to every engine below, so that no module of the CLI package ever learns that a type has a configuration. The result is a project type in its own right: `projectTypeProblems` holds it to the same shape, it keeps the identifier of the type that built it, and it may declare only capabilities the unconfigured type named in `capabilities` or in the new `configurableCapabilities` - otherwise `codkit types`, which runs with no patch set in reach, would print a matrix the tool does not keep. `codkit types` prints both sets and carries both in `--json` (`CMD-TYPES`). Where the boundaries of a watch pass are is the one answer that used to be a path into the type's package and cannot be for a configured type; `BuildArea` therefore takes `watchProfilePath: string | null` beside an optional `watchProfile` carrying the same document as data, and the engine validates the data with the schema it applies to the file (PROP-010 `PASS-BOUNDARIES-ARE-DATA`). Added on 2026-09-09 with the second official type, by the rule of `DECISION-TYPE-CONTRACT-FROM-MEASUREMENT`. @status:spec/done

**What the engine never knows.** No module of the CLI package names a type's fact: no `product.json`, no `src/vs/`, no `extensions/`, no `registerSingleton`, no `npm run hygiene`, no icon table. The graft budget, the marker grammar, the drift guard's predicate, the sacrifice by name of `--discard`, the licence carriers, the generated branch, the cycle's transactions and the standards protocol belong to the engine and are forbidden to consult the type. A grep of the CLI package for the VS Code tokens of DESIGN-001 §1 is a gate of phase P2 and prints zero. The gate is **executable and part of the floor**: the dictionary and the scan live in the engine's own suite, because the one constant that slipped past the hand-run gate (##TYPE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS) slipped past it precisely by not being in a list anybody could re-read. The list may only grow. @status:spec/done
3. Types are packages

Workspace layout of the tool repository: `packages/codkit` (the CLI and the engine; the binary `codkit`), `packages/type-api` (the contract), `packages/type-vscode`, `packages/type-generic`, `packages/type-theia`. Each package has its own `package.json`, tests and licence carriers; the floor runs over the workspace. The split happens once, in phase P2, and every later type is born as a package. @status:spec/done

The engine holds a **registry of the package names it will load**, keyed by type identifier (`vscode` → `@codkit/type-vscode`). A type is resolved by a dynamic import of that package from the CLI package's own dependencies; the official types are regular dependencies of the CLI package. No module is loaded from a patch set or from an arbitrary path: determinism, the air-gapped circuit and the clean room all want the set of loadable code fixed by the tool's own release. Adding a type is publishing its package and adding its name to the registry. @status:spec/done

A `type` the registry does not know, or whose package is not installed, is `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`, exit 2, naming the identifier and the package the registry expected; no command proceeds without a type. @status:spec/done

The air-gapped supply kit (PROP-011) carries the CLI package and every official type package as tarballs; `npm pack` of the workspace produces them; the kit's manifest lists them with their versions and hashes. @status:spec/done

The P2-4 implementation: `npm run kit` (`tools/build-supply-kit.mjs`) packs every published package of the workspace into `target/supply-kit/` and writes `kit-manifest.json` beside them - `codkitSupplyKit: 1`, the version of the CLI package, and one row per tarball with the package name, its version, the type identifier it implements (from the registry), its role (`cli`, `contract`, `type`), the file name, the size and the sha256; the build refuses when the registry names a type package the workspace does not publish, so a registered type can never be missing from a kit. The kit is installed as ONE unit - the manifest carries the exact command, `npm install --offline ./codkit-<version>.tgz ./codkit-type-*-<version>.tgz …` in an empty directory - because the type tarballs are what the CLI package's dependencies on them resolve against with no registry in reach; installing the CLI tarball alone asks the registry for `@codkit/type-api` and fails. `bundleDependencies` was tried and does not apply: npm does not bundle a workspace dependency, which is a symlink at pack time. The tarballs carry `npm-shrinkwrap.json` for the THIRD-PARTY closure only (`codkit`, `@codkit/type-api`, `@codkit/type-vscode`); the sibling `@codkit/*` packages are deliberately absent from those files, since a resolved registry URL for them would send an air-gapped install out of the circuit, and the kit manifest is what pins them instead. The third-party half of the delivery is unchanged (PROP-011 ##SK-CODKIT-NPM): an internal registry or a pre-filled npm cache; with neither, the offline install stops at the first third-party package with npm's `ENOTCACHED`. @status:impl/done

`@codkit/type-api` is the only import a type package may take from the tool; the CLI package imports the type only through the interface. A change of the interface is a change of every official type in the same commit of the workspace (the workspace is one repository precisely so that this stays atomic). The contract package is not purely declarative: it carries the codec of its own payload format (PNG, the language of `ImagePayload`) and the shape of a refusal, because one implementation must serve the engine and every type alike; a container codec of one upstream family (ICNS, ICO) belongs to that family's type. Decision of 2026-09-09 after the extraction; a fourth package for shared pixels was considered and rejected as a package for one file. @status:spec/done
4. Configuration

`codkit.json` schema 2 has `"type": "<identifier>"` and `"typeConfig": { ... }`. The engine validates the universal fields; the type validates `typeConfig` with its own schema and refuses with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the field. One patch set, one type. @status:spec/done

Schema 2 is the only schema: a `codkit.json` without `type` (schema 1) is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` that names the two fields to add (`type`, `typeConfig.ownRoot`) and nothing else; no command reads schema 1 and no code path infers a type. There is one consumer of the tool today and it is migrated in the campaign (phase P2: its `codkit.json` gets `"type": "vscode"` and `"typeConfig": {"ownRoot": "src/vs/patchset"}`, and its gates - `verify`, `status`, `ci --profile build`, the static proof, the dev and package UI proofs - run on the migrated configuration). Owner ruling of 2026-09-09. @status:spec/done

The own root is a **full path from the tree root** in `typeConfig.ownRoot`; the field is required, the type supplies its constraints (VS Code: under `src/vs/`; Theia: a workspace package directory) and refuses a root outside them with `CK-E-CONFIG`. The engine treats the own root as an opaque directory: mirrored by content, excluded from the drift guard, named in the inventory. `typeConfig.ownRoot` is the first of the owned directories; a type that owns more names the others in its own `typeConfig` fields (Theia: `applicationRoot`), and the engine treats every owned directory the same way. @status:spec/done

Several forks are several patch sets, each bound to its own fork tree per command (`--patches-dir`, `--fork-dir`, the local config), exactly as today (`GOAL-ANY-FORK`). Two forks of one upstream are two patch sets of one type; forks of different upstreams are patch sets of different types. Sharing between forks travels through packages (standards, runtime, skills), never through the tool's configuration. A workspace file naming several patch sets is a later convenience and is not part of phases P1-P5. @status:spec/done
5. CLI

The verbs of the roster (PROP-007 `COMMAND-ROSTER`) are universal and keep their names, flags and exit codes. Their output names the type where it matters: `where` prints it, the JSON envelope carries `codkit.type`. @status:spec/done

A verb that needs a capability the type does not declare refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, exit 2, naming the type and the capability, before any write; no verb silently does something else. The verbs that need one: `imageset *` (`brand-images`), `gen brand` (`gen-brand`), `build *` (`build-channels`), `runtime load|check` (`runtime-library`), and `verify` over an artifact of a layer the type does not provide. @status:spec/done

`codkit types` - print the registered types, their package and version, and the capability matrix; `--json`: `data: {types: [{id, package, version, installed, capabilities, configurableCapabilities}]}`. `configurableCapabilities` is the abilities a type declares only for a patch set whose `typeConfig` asks for them (`TYPE-CONFIGURED`); it is empty for a type that answers the same thing for every patch set, and the human output prints it as a `from typeConfig:` line under the declared ones. Read-only, no patch set required. @status:spec/done

New codes: `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN` (type not registered or package not installed), `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` (verb or layer outside the type's capabilities). A type may add codes only under its own prefix (`CK-E-VSCODE-…`) for facts the engine cannot state; every code has an FAQ entry (PROP-012). @status:spec/done
6. The official types

`vscode` - today's behaviour, extracted without change: the specification module `modules/vscode` holds its answers (layout `src/vs/<own>` and `extensions/`, the `product.json` overlay with the `product.overrides.json` dev channel, built-in extensions, `registerSingleton`, `workbench.common.main`, `npm ci`/hygiene/eslint/watch channels/`test-node`, the package build and its stamps, the advisory readers, the brand image set, the runtime library, the seam catalogue, the conventions). The product's gates - `verify`, `status`, `ci --profile build`, its static proof and UI proofs - are the regression net of the extraction. @status:spec/plan

`generic` - a plain git upstream with no product model: no extensions, no service overrides, no entry module, no dev channel, no brand images, no runtime library; the install, lint, compile and test commands are declared in `typeConfig`; the own root is a configured directory. It carries `own`, `patch`, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule` and `config-overlay` over declared JSON targets without a dev channel, so that `load|save|verify|cycle|publish|ci` run over any upstream before its own type exists. Its polygon is a **synthetic repository** in the fixtures (owner ruling). @status:spec/done

The P3 implementation of `TYPE-GENERIC`: `@codkit/type-generic`, whose whole knowledge is the section `typeConfig` of the patch set that declares it - `ownRoot` (any directory of the tree; only a path that is not repository-relative POSIX is refused), `commands.install` and `commands.lint` (argv, written as a string split on whitespace or as the words themselves), `commands.compile` (the watch channels: the npm script of each and where a pass begins and ends in its output), `commands.test` (`{command, ownGlobArg?}`, run over the glob `<ownRoot>/**/*.test.*`), `overlayTargets` (the JSON files an overlay may touch, never with a development channel), `cleanupWhitelist` and `identity.manifest` (`{path, nameField?}`, the fingerprint of a healthy tree). The unconfigured type declares NO capability and names `config-overlay` and `build-channels` as configurable; `configure` declares `config-overlay` when a target was declared and `build-channels` when a channel was, so `imageset`, `gen brand`, `runtime load|check` always refuse with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, and `build *` refuses until compile channels are declared. The channels carry their pass boundaries because the engine's profile schema requires them and the tool never guesses them (PROP-010 `PASS-BOUNDARIES-ARE-DATA`): a bare list of script names would produce a profile that recognizes no pass. The type ships no data file, delivers no standards package, declares no advisory reader - the cycle's advisory then reports the two pins and no semantic change - and its feature skeleton is identifiers, feature and test inside one directory with no composition root to register into. @status:impl/done

`theia` - the second real type, designed from the facts of Theia master (`research/theia-facts-<version>`) and specified in `modules/theia`: the own root as a workspace package, the application manifest as the overlay target, inversify `rebind` as the service override, the application's module list as the entry module, yarn/lerna build and watch, its test runner, electron-builder packaging, its advisory readers. It is proved by a real product of the owner built on it, in that product's own repository, the way the VS Code product was built. @status:spec/done

The P5 implementation: `@codkit/type-theia`, a **configured** type (##TYPE-CONFIGURED) whose section carries the three answers upstream cannot give - `ownRoot` (a workspace package directory under `packages/*`, `dev-packages/*` or `examples/*`), `ownPackageName` (what `lerna run <script> --scope` selects) and `applicationRoot` (the application whose `package.json` is the overlay target), plus the optional names of the two root npm scripts that are its watch channels. Its capabilities are the same for every patch set - `config-overlay`, `service-override`, `build-channels`, `upgrade-advisory` - so `codkit types` prints a true matrix with no configuration in reach, and `configurableCapabilities` is empty. Four capabilities of the roster are absent and each absence is an answer: no `entry-module` (own code is included by one line of the application's `dependencies`), no `own-extensions` (a Theia extension **is** own code), no `brand-images` (upstream has no icon target table), no `gen-brand` (identity is a manifest key, not a string funnel), no `dev-channel` and no `runtime-library` yet. Two things the second type measured and the contract grew for it: `TreeFingerprint.contentProblem`, because this family is proved by what two manifests say and not only by their presence (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-008#ID-CHECK-FINGERPRINTS`), and `ServiceOverrideVerifier.overrideProblems`, because a `rebind` wins only when the own package depends on the package that binds the service and the engine cannot state that edge itself. Both are optional members: the first two types are unchanged by them. @status:impl/done
7. Testing

The engine's tests run against a **stub type** in the fixtures that answers the contract with the smallest possible layout, and the pseudo-upstream is shaped by that stub's layout (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-013#FIXTURE-UPSTREAM`); the e2e suites, which drive the real CLI, reach it through `TYPE-TEST-SEAM`. They never import an official type, with one kind of exception that is an answer rather than a gap: a suite about a payload the tool ships for one family - its runtime library, its brand images, its vibe packages - and the suite of the registry itself are that family's polygon inside the engine's tree, and each such file says so in its own header. Each type package has its own suites and its own polygon; FEAT-001 becomes two polygons - the VS Code-shaped one it is today and the synthetic generic one. @status:spec/done

The engine's e2e suites run the real CLI as a subprocess, and that subprocess resolves a type only through the registry of `TYPE-REGISTRY`; a stub type living in the test tree is therefore unreachable to it. The test build alone (the build condition `codkit-test`, modelled on `CODKIT_TEST_STANDARDS_SOURCE`, `CODKIT_TEST_RUNTIME_SOURCE` and `CODKIT_TEST_CRASH_AT`) honours the env `CODKIT_TEST_TYPE_PACKAGE=<id>=<absolute path of a module exporting projectType>`, which adds that one type to the registry for the lifetime of the process; the module must answer the contract the way any package does, and the row never appears in `codkit types` of a production build. Without the build condition the variable is ignored and the same `type` is `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`, and a test proves that the seam does not leak, the way S33 proves it for the standards source. The production registry is unchanged: nothing is ever loaded from a patch set or from a path named in `codkit.json`. @status:spec/done

Acceptance scenarios (FEAT-002): a schema-1 patch set is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming `type` and `typeConfig.ownRoot`; the migrated VS Code patch set behaves exactly as before; `codkit types` lists the official types; `imageset` over a `generic` patch set refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`; a `type` the registry does not know refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`; the generic polygon passes `load`, `save`, `verify`, `cycle` and `ci --profile verify` end to end; the VS Code polygon passes every scenario it passed before the split. @status:spec/plan
8. Specifications: the split

`modules/codkit` specifies the engine and this contract; `modules/vscode` specifies the `vscode` type; `modules/theia` will specify the `theia` type; `common/*` states the vision without naming an upstream. A fact that is a type's answer moves to the type's module; a fact about the engine stays. @status:spec/plan

Anchors are immutable: a moved fact leaves a tombstone at its old address naming the new one (`NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR`), and every `##ANCHOR` citation in code is re-pointed in the same commit; `trace:check` and the spec map are the gates. The unit count of the two modules together equals the count before the split plus the tombstones and the new facts of this document. @status:spec/plan
The type modules of the tool are English like the rest of the tool's specifications (`SPEC-LANGUAGE-IS-ENGLISH`); a product's specifications keep the product's own rule. @status:spec/plan
Installation registry integrity

The published installation owns config/type-registry.json, schema codkitTypeRegistry:1. Entries pin id, npm package/version, contractVersion, manifestSha256, literal integrityRoots and path/sha256 receipts for every npm-packed type file. The reader rejects malformed/duplicate registrations and reads no registry from cwd, patchset or environment. Every non-test type validates identity and manifest digest, proves each approved file through contained I/O, and refuses unapproved additions under its publication roots before dynamic adapter import. Dependencies outside the type package remain the separately supplied installation closure; this is not a sandbox for trusted executable code or a defence against a concurrent trusted-root writer. @status:impl/done

A source developer explicitly approves byte updates through npm run types:refresh; runtime:build refreshes the receipts after deterministic compilation. types:check recomputes npm's publication list without lifecycle scripts and fails stale receipts without rewriting them. It preserves registry entry order and never adds a package implicitly. Runtime cannot refresh approvals. External administrator overlays and signature custody remain the external-type supply stage; this shipped registry does not load arbitrary modules or weaken that boundary. @status:impl/done
Declarative type handshake

Every installed type exports `./type-manifest.json`: strict JSON data with `typeManifestVersion`, `contractVersion`, `id`, npm `package` and `version`, `engineRange` (`min` inclusive, `maxExclusive` exclusive), `capabilities` and `configurableCapabilities`. Manifest and contract version 1 are required independently of package version. Package identity agrees with its installed package.json, capability names are closed and unique, and the stable engine version lies in a non-empty interval. A malformed, unsupported or foreign declaration refuses with CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN and expected/actual context before dynamic adapter import. Stable three-component versions are the supported interval vocabulary; prerelease negotiation requires an explicit future contract. @status:impl/done

`codkit types` reads declarative manifests without evaluating adapters. Its rows add `manifestVersion`, `contractVersion`, `manifestSha256`, `source` and `problem` to the existing fields. `installed` reports a compatible installed declaration, not functional adapter conformance. `source` is installation or test-seam. Manifest sha256 is an inspection identity only; adapter-content integrity is a separate trusted-registry obligation. First executable resolution checks the adapter's functional contract and both capability sets against its declaration. @status:impl/done

An authorized test module has a strict declaration at `<module-path>.manifest.json`, with fixture identity @codkit/test-stub version 1.0.0. It passes the same version/engine/capability validator as installation packages. The existing codkit-test condition remains mandatory; production never widens its registry through environment input. @status:impl/done

The contract package ships `codkit-type-conform <type-package-directory>` for a separate type repository. It reads manifest data first, then executes the operator-selected ESM exports["."].import adapter contained in that package and checks functional answers and declaration consistency. This authoring tool is distinct from read-only registry inspection and does not authorize patchset-controlled executable supply. @status:impl/done

Decision: use an explicit stable-version interval for engine compatibility. Why: all current packages use stable 1.0.0; an inclusive lower/exclusive upper interval is enough for the measured handshake and avoids introducing unneeded range syntax. Considered and rejected: a permissive arbitrary version string (cannot enforce compatibility), a full range-language dependency before a prerelease consumer exists (adds unsupported semantics). When to revisit: a released type needs prerelease engines or multiple disjoint supported ranges. @status:impl/done
9. Decisions

**Decision:** a type is a separate npm package from the first day, resolved through a registry of names. **Why:** the owner's ruling - the procedure of splitting is done once; a package boundary that exists only in a directory drifts back into the engine. **Considered and rejected:** in-tree directories under one package (cheaper now, a second split later); arbitrary plugin loading from a patch set (breaks determinism, the air-gapped kit and the clean room). **When to revisit:** a third party ships a type - then the registry becomes a declared list in the tool's configuration rather than a constant. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** no compatibility layer for the old configuration schema: schema 2 is required, schema 1 is refused with a migration hint. **Why:** the owner's ruling of 2026-09-09 - the tool has one consumer, and fixing it is cheaper than building a compatibility layer and maintaining it afterwards; the consumer is migrated inside the campaign with its gates as the proof. **Considered and rejected:** reading schema 1 as `vscode` (a second code path, a second set of tests, and a rule that would outlive its only reason). **When to revisit:** never for schema 1; a future schema change gets the same treatment while the consumers can be counted on one hand. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the contract's areas are the measured variation points and nothing else. **Why:** an interface designed for one real type fits that type; the `generic` type and the Theia type are the two forces that keep it honest, and each new question is added when a type needs it. **Considered and rejected:** a general "hooks everywhere" plugin API (speculative surface, untestable). **When to revisit:** a third real type that needs a tenth question. @status:spec/plan

**Decision:** the layout area answers with a list of owned directories and with the build outputs inside them, not with one own root. **Why:** measured on the second real type (P5, 2026-09-09): a Theia package compiles `src/` to `lib/` inside itself, so the engine that treats the whole owned directory as source read a build as a change of own code and refused to load; and the product's application is a second owned directory the engine mirrored nothing of. **Considered and rejected:** compiling own code elsewhere (fights the family's own tools and lint); listing the outputs in the cleanup whitelist only (they would still count as changed own code). **When to revisit:** a family whose outputs are interleaved with sources file by file rather than by directory. @status:spec/done
PROP-017: Public format coverage and compatibility inventory
Public format catalog

The machine-readable compatibility inventory is `public-formats.json` beside this contract. Each row identifies a format, its owner, trust boundary, current schema version, compatibility, migration or refusal rule, fingerprint participation, governing contract and conformance test paths. The underlying contract and reader govern behavior; the catalog records that behavior and does not authorize a format migration. @status:impl/done

A seam without an independent numeric version carries `version: null` and an explicit `versionGap` explaining the inherited version or the outstanding compatibility work. A missing version is never silently assigned version 1. A test path records existing coverage, not a claim that every requirement has a conformance test; `testGap` records known incomplete evidence. @status:impl/done

`npm run formats:check` lists formats and refuses a missing compatibility/migration policy, source/test evidence, duplicate identity or observed schema-version drift. Discovery scans TypeScript and JavaScript declarations, literal validators and object writers with `codkit`-prefixed property names in all package source directories and production tools, without executing them. Non-JSON seams, nested schema fields and manual validators are explicitly registered; named numeric version constants are checked against source. @status:impl/done

Discovery is a coverage tripwire for the established property and constant conventions, not an arbitrary program analyzer. A new format using computed keys, aliased validators, another version-field convention or dynamic version expressions requires an explicit catalog entry and discovery extension with a failing fixture. A compatibility checker does not replace runtime parser conformance tests. @status:impl/done

Changing a catalog row's version or migration policy requires reading its governing contract and reviewing the reader/writer change together. Catalog maintenance does not change serialized patchsets, delta fingerprints, generated history, executable type trust or licence policy. @status:impl/done
PROP-018: Immutable component release descriptors
Descriptor data and integrity

A component release is a strict root object carrying descriptorSha256 and codkitComponentRelease:1, componentId, package/publish operation, immutable upstream revision and optional human label/resolution/provenance, patchset commit and config digest, declared type package/version/contract/manifest digest, discipline, generated commit/tree, artifact receipts, build recipe digest, selected licence-policy receipts, and distribution requirements/evidence. Unknown fields and unsupported versions refuse. SHA-256 receipt values and Git commit/tree object IDs are distinct types and algorithms; a Git object ID is never represented as a SHA-256 file digest. @status:impl/done

Field order follows the single Zod schema. Artifacts and policies are sorted by identity; distribution lists are sorted by requirement using UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate identities, escaping artifact paths, empty distribution requirements and inconsistent completeness/missing lists refuse. descriptorSha256 hashes the canonical compact JSON of every root field except descriptorSha256 itself, including the format version. The stored descriptor is deterministic two-space UTF-8 JSON, LF-only, without BOM and with exactly one final LF. Readers validate the digest and exact canonical bytes; no migration or adapter execution is implied by reading a descriptor. @status:impl/done

Receipts live at the contained patchset runtime path .codkit/releases/<descriptorSha256>.json. A writer validates data before I/O and publishes complete bytes only at an absent path through the existing atomic exclusive-link capability. Retrying identical bytes is idempotent; existing conflicting bytes, symlink parents/leaves and filename/body digest mismatch refuse without replacing the foreign file. This content digest establishes byte integrity, not origin authentication, legal compatibility, signing custody or authorization to deliver a release. @status:impl/done

Artifact capture reads real selected outputs under a single physical root. Regular-file SHA-256 uses the existing contained descriptor proof and 64 KiB streaming buffer, with size/mtime/ctime stability checks. It returns absence for missing files, never an invented digest. Artifact paths and parents are contained; inode/mode/metadata checks refuse substitutions. Symlinks are represented by their exact UTF-8 link text bytes, never by following their target; a target escaping the physical root refuses. @status:impl/done

A directory digest is SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON {codkitArtifactTree:1, entries:[...]}. Entries sort by UTF-8 path bytes; the root has path empty, and each entry names kind and permission mode masked by 07777. Empty directories are included. File/link entries additionally carry SHA-256 and payload byte count. Directory bytes is the sum of those payload counts, not a fictional archive size. This canonical tree stream is distinct from hashing a physical archive file; changing its rules requires coordinated descriptor/tree-format compatibility review. @status:impl/done

Release fact capture proves configured upstream SHA/commit-date against actual Git objects and reads immutable generated commit/tree objects, effective canonical config, the explicitly supplied validated type declaration and a fresh validated installed supply-policy snapshot. Component identity defaults to the digest of sorted patchset history roots; shallow history requires an explicit component identifier. Recipe identity hashes JSON data without executing it. Missing organization policy, distribution notices or SBOM remain missing evidence, never invented approvals. Dirty package checkout and absent physical package artifacts remain explicit missing requirements alongside real Git object receipts. @status:impl/done

The public package release operation verifies selected type/declaration identity before packaging, observes completed outputs before the existing unconditional scratch/overlay restoration, and publishes its descriptor only after restoration succeeds. It refuses a changed generated commit or patchset commit. Failed packaging/restore emits no successful descriptor. Artifact receipts are checked again after restoration; changed delivered bytes refuse instead of recording a stale pre-restoration digest. CLI package exposes the receipt path, digest, evidence status and missing requirements. --component-id supplies a stable explicit identity, including shallow repositories. The lower-level packaging worker remains available for established library callers and fixtures; release recording is a library capability rather than CLI-only logic. @status:impl/done

The public publish receipt capability captures facts from the selected immutable patchset commit and the disposable checked checkout before delivery. The checked generated tip remains distinct from shaped/squashed/orphan delivered Git objects. Successful export/ref delivery records an immutable historical delivery receipt after the existing lease/tag transaction finishes and the disposable checkout is released; a failed gate or tag collision has no successful descriptor. Repeating an up-to-date immutable release is deterministic. Local receipt failure after delivery reports that delivery already succeeded and requests repair/retry; no cross-repository rollback or signing/legal approval is implied. Explicit type declarations come from a composition root or trusted registry, never patchset executable data. @status:impl/done

Completeness is relative to the explicit selected policy requirements and their actual evidence receipts. Emitters must obtain hashes from the objects and bytes they observed, name the licence-policy scope, retain unavailable evidence as missing and avoid inventing an external approval. The schema alone cannot attest how facts were obtained. Package/publish integration must bind the descriptor to the exact checked inputs and preserve package restore, publish leases, immutable tags and existing operation refusal behavior. @status:spec/done

Implement the source proposal's single-component release descriptor before a coordinator. Use a content-addressed immutable receipt rather than a mutable latest-release pointer: deterministic retries can compare exact bytes and conflicting data remains inspectable. Do not introduce signatures or organization commercial rulings without the corresponding external inputs. Revisit distribution requirements when P0.10 supplies trusted organization enforcement and real artifact evidence. @status:impl/done
PROP-019: Organization consumer licensing and distribution evidence
Separate authorities and controlled expressions

codkitOrganizationPolicy:1 declares organization profile ID/revision, own holders and license expression, approved/forbidden third-party expressions, approved exceptions, a LicenseRef namespace, exact canonical custom-license texts with SHA-256, distribution notice/SBOM/carrier requirements and optional legal-review reference. The schema is strict and types derive from it. SPDX identifiers come from the installed list. NOASSERTION, undeclared/foreign-namespace LicenseRef and missing/changed text/hash refuse. Custom texts are LF-only with a final LF and no BOM. This profile applies to consumer scope and never weakens Codkit's separate installed supply policy. @status:impl/done

A user/admin composition root supplies the policy directory; the default is the user .codkit directory. organization-policies.json carries codkitOrganizationPolicyStore:1 and policy records. Store reads use contained regular-file I/O, validate every profile and refuse conflicting IDs including case aliases. A directory inside the physical patchset or an alias resolving into it refuses. No cwd/patchset fallback or patchset-supplied policy path is accepted. The selected policy and raw store bytes each receive their own digest; a digest is not an invented signature or legal approval. @status:impl/done

Patchset selection contains only profile ID and optional additionalForbidden expressions. Holders, allowlists, license text, policy locations and other authority fields refuse. Additional prohibitions are monotone and cannot enable a license. Own scope uses the exact declared own expression; third-party scope uses exact approved expression combinations and forbidden identifiers/expressions. AND/OR/WITH and bounded parentheses are syntax, never automatic inference of legal permissions; an OR combination not explicitly approved remains refused. @status:impl/done

Consumer source scanning, actual artifact NOTICE/carrier checks and selected SBOM export must bind the selected trusted policy before package/publish enforcement is accepted. A minified artifact without required attached notice is incomplete/red even when source headers were valid. Report evidence complete/incomplete, never a legal-compatibility ruling. Mechanism fixtures are labelled examples, not real commercial approvals or external partner evidence. @status:spec/done
theia PROP-001: The `theia` project type - overview and module map

`theia` is the project type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`) that carries the tool's knowledge of the Eclipse Theia monorepo as an upstream: an npm workspace of packages on Node 24, built by lerna and tsc project references and bundled by esbuild, composed at build time from one application `package.json` by inversify container modules. It is the second real type and the proof of the contract: it answers the nine questions with different shapes than the `vscode` type, and some of its answers are absences. @status:spec/done

Every fact of this module is derived from `research/theia-facts-1.75.0/` (upstream master `c8926e4d`, 2026-09-08, version 1.75.0) and cites its file; a fact the spike did not establish is marked as an open question, not guessed (`research/theia-facts-1.75.0/open-questions.md`). @status:spec/done
1. Module map

PROP-001 the type and this map; PROP-002 upstream identity and tree layout; PROP-003 layers - the application manifest overlay, the own package, service overrides by `rebind`, no entry-module graft; PROP-004 build, watch, lint, test and packaging; PROP-005 upgrade advisory, hygiene and conventions; PROP-006 the absences - no brand images, no runtime library, no build-time stamps, no upstream packaging - and what a product supplies instead. @status:spec/done
3. The packages of the type

The type names one vibe package of its own, `seams-theia` - the catalogue of the seams this family of upstreams offers, ranked from a pull request upstream down to the internals of a module. `codkit standards load` delivers it beside the universal `standards` and `agent-skills` to a patch set of this type and to no other (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-014#STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`). What the catalogue says that its counterpart of the first type cannot: in this family an **addition needs no upstream edit at all**, so its two highest tiers reach further and a patch of an upstream file is a rare event that the product's seam map has to justify. The agent skills stay type-neutral and route to whichever catalogue the declared type delivers. @status:spec/done
2. Capabilities

Declared: `config-overlay` (targets: the application `package.json`; no `dev-channel`), `service-override` (inversify `rebind` in an own container module), `build-channels` (`tsc -b -w` and `theia build --watch`), `upgrade-advisory`. Not declared in the first version: `own-extensions` (a Theia extension is own code itself - see PROP-003; VS Code-style plugins are a later capability `own-plugins`), `entry-module` (Theia needs no graft to include own code), `brand-images`, `gen-brand`, `runtime-library`. A verb that needs an undeclared capability refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`). @status:spec/done
theia PROP-002: Upstream identity and tree layout
1. Upstream identity

Release tags match `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`; the rolling tag `next` is mutable and a pin resolver ignores it (`01-version-and-sha.md`, tag shape). A pin is `tag@sha@date` as everywhere; a pin on a master commit between tags is allowed and is written with the nearest reachable tag plus the sha (`v1.75.0@c8926e4d…`). @status:spec/done

The upstream version is read from `lerna.json` (`version`, fixed mode), not from the root `package.json`, which is the private `@theia/monorepo` at `0.0.0`; every `@theia/*` package carries the same literal version (`01`, "Where the version is written"). @status:spec/done

`check-tree` fingerprints: root `package.json` named `@theia/monorepo` with `workspaces` covering `packages/*` and `dev-packages/*`; `lerna.json` with `npmClient: "npm"`; `packages/core/package.json` named `@theia/core` at the version of `lerna.json`; the anchor commit reachable from the pin (`01`, `02`). @status:spec/done
2. Tree layout

The own root is a workspace package directory: `typeConfig.ownRoot` defaults to `packages/<name>` and must match one of the workspace globs of the root `package.json` (`dev-packages/*`, `packages/*`, `examples/*`); the type refuses a root outside them (`CK-E-CONFIG`). A package under `packages/` is what the `theiaext` scripts, the generated tsconfig references and the `nls-extract` glob already cover (`10-downstream-own-package.md`, "Placement"). @status:spec/done

The own root is an npm package with `theiaExtensions` (the ten entry kinds of `extension-package.ts:22-33`), `version` equal to the monorepo version, `dependencies` on the `@theia/*` packages it uses at the exact same version, the `theiaext` scripts (`lint`, `build`, `watch`, `clean`, `compile`, `test`) and `@theia/ext-scripts` as a dev dependency, its own `.eslintrc.js` and `tsconfig.json` (a package without them is not linted at all - `08`); the skeleton of `examples/api-provider-sample/package.json` is the reference (`10`, "The skeleton"). @status:spec/done

A product's application is a second directory the delta owns, `typeConfig.applicationRoot` (default `applications/<name>` or an `examples/*` slot), whose `package.json` is the overlay target of PROP-003. The type materializes both directories the way the `vscode` type materializes its own root: mirrored by content from the delta, excluded from the drift guard. **Implemented in P5-2** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT`): the type answers `layout.ownRoots` with the own package (role `own`) and the application (role `application`), the delta keeps the second one under `delta/own-roots/application/`, and inside it **the pin is the boundary** - the files the pin ships there (the manifest of a forked example application, its tsconfig) stay upstream's and are changed by the config-overlay, resource-file or patch layer, while everything the pin does not ship is own code of that directory. That is what lets the overlay of the manifest and the ownership of the directory co-exist, and it is what an application written from scratch needs nothing of: at a pin that ships nothing there, the delta owns the whole directory. @status:spec/done

**Superseded by P5-2 for its second half** (the delta now materializes the application directory; see the fact above). The P5 implementation was: `typeConfig.applicationRoot` is a required field and it is what the type builds its overlay target, its package build and its advisory reader of the application from. The second half of the fact above - the delta *materializing* that directory the way it materializes the own root - is **not** implemented and is not expressible in the contract as it stands: the engine mirrors exactly one own root (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`), and a second mirrored directory is a change of the engine, not of a type. What a product does today instead: it forks one of upstream's example applications, points `applicationRoot` at that directory as it exists **at the pin**, and owns its content through the overlay of its manifest and through resource-file artifacts. An application written from scratch, which exists at no pin, cannot be an overlay target at all (`OVERLAY-BASE-IS-THE-PIN`), and is the open question this fact leaves for the phase that needs it. P5-2 answered exactly that: the engine mirrors every owned directory, and an application that exists at no pin is owned whole. @status:impl/done

The untracked content the fresh pass **keeps**; everything outside the list it removes (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#CLEANUP-WHITELIST-CONTENT`): `node_modules/`, `**/lib/` of workspace packages, `**/src-gen/`, `**/gen-esbuild.*.mjs` and `**/gen-webpack*.js` if present, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`, `.browser_modules/`, `**/.nyc_output/`, `**/coverage/`, `**/dist/` written by the packager the product runs after the build, `plugins/` downloaded by `theia download:plugins` (`02-repository-layout.md`, runtime folders and build outputs). The generated bundler entries are `gen-esbuild.{browser,node,electron}.mjs` since 1.75.0 and the `gen-webpack*` name is the leftover of the build that was removed; the user-editable `esbuild.mjs` of an application is **not** in the list, because a build only regenerates it when it is gone (measured in P5). @status:spec/done

**The packager of the product writes into `<applicationRoot>/dist/`, and that is a build output of the owned application directory.** Upstream has no packager, so no fact of upstream named the directory; the first real consumer of this type ran one after `theia build` (##THEIA-PACKAGE-BUILD) and got 700 MiB of unpacked application, AppImage and archive inside a directory the delta owns. The engine read every file of it as own code the tree had and the delta did not - `status` printed 80-odd `tree-edited` paths and `load` refused with `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` - while `lib/` and `src-gen/` beside it were passed over, because those were named and this was not. `dist/**` therefore joins the build outputs of the application (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT`): the mirror never copies it, `status` never counts it, a plain `load` leaves it where the packager put it, and `load --fresh` removes it - exactly the rule the other outputs of that directory follow. Outside an owned directory the same output is on the cleanup whitelist and survives a fresh pass, as `**/lib/` and `**/src-gen/` do. @status:impl/done

**The install of this family compiles a native addon, and its output is on the list too: `dev-packages/ffmpeg/build/`.** Exactly one package of the monorepo carries a `binding.gyp` - `dev-packages/ffmpeg`, the proprietary-codec check of the Electron distribution (`11-release-packaging.md`) - and `npm ci` builds it there through the `node-gyp install` preinstall step (`03-build-watch-lint-test.md`). The directory is untracked, so a fresh pass took it with the rest of the litter; the next bundle of the application then died on `Cannot find module '../build/Debug/ffmpeg.node'` and the only recovery was a full `npm ci`. Measured by the first real consumer of this type on a real clone: 124 untracked paths were removed and this was one of them. The entry names that one package rather than every directory called `build`, because a `build/` anywhere else in this tree is not the output of an install and the discipline of the list is that what is not on it goes away. @status:impl/done

Never patched: `dev-packages/cli/patches/**` (upstream's own patches of `node_modules`, applied on every install by `theia-patch`), `package-lock.json` (regenerated by install), `src-gen/**` (generated). A patch of `lerna.json` or of the root `package.json` workspace globs is a graft of the constant set and needs a decision record. @status:spec/done

Marker comment forms are the engine's by extension; Theia adds none. The SPDX header rule of upstream's lint applies to every `.ts`/`.tsx` under a linted package (PROP-005), which shapes where a marker block may sit in an own file: below the header. @status:spec/done
theia PROP-003: Layers - the application manifest, the own package, rebind
1. config-overlay: the application manifest

The overlay target is the application's `package.json`: the `theia` section (`target`, `frontend.config` with `applicationName`, preference defaults, `electron` window options and `appUserModelId`, `backend.config`), `productName`, `main`, `theiaPluginsDir`, `theiaPlugins` and the `dependencies` inventory of extensions (`05-application-and-product-model.md`; schema `application-props.ts:286-336`). There is no `product.json` and no dev channel: what the running application reads was frozen into `src-gen/` at build time, so there is no sidecar to read instead of the target. **Measured in P5 and corrected here**: a target without a dev channel is written by `overlay apply` and by the build materialization of the cycle, never by `load` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OVERLAY-TWO-CHANNELS`); `load` leaves the manifest as the pin has it, which is also what keeps the upstream gates seeing the unmaterialized tree. The type also declares the **root** manifest as a second target, restricted to `scripts`, because the watch channels of this family are npm scripts of the tree root (PROP-004 `THEIA-BUILD-CHANNELS`) and the workspace globs beside them are a graft of the constant set (PROP-002 `THEIA-FORBIDDEN-TARGETS`). @status:spec/done

Because the application directory is owned by the delta (PROP-002 `THEIA-APPLICATION-ROOT`), the overlay's `expectUpstream` is checked against upstream's example application the product forked from (`examples/electron/package.json` or `examples/browser/package.json`) when the product declares one as its origin, and against nothing when the application is written from scratch; the drift detector reports the origin's drift as information, not as a refusal. **Measured in P5**: the universal overlay machinery reads the base of every target from the pin, so `applicationRoot` names the forked example application as it exists at the pin, and `expectUpstream` is checked against that file; an application that exists at no pin is outside the layer (see `THEIA-APPLICATION-ROOT-IMPL`). @status:spec/done

Product identity is one key, `theia.frontend.config.applicationName`, frozen into `src-gen/frontend/index.js` at build time and read at runtime through `FrontendApplicationConfigProvider.get()` (`05`; `frontend-generator.ts:80-82`); the page title and the Electron window title come from it (`09-build-time-stamps.md`). A brand transform over upstream strings is therefore not needed for the name; it is needed only if a product wants to rename upstream's own vocabulary, and then it is a graft of the localization funnel of PROP-005. @status:spec/done
2. own: the package that needs no graft

Own code enters the application by one line in the application's `dependencies` plus `theiaExtensions` in the own package: the generator collects extension packages by module resolution (`extension-package-collector.ts:64`) and emits `await load(container, require(...))` for each (`frontend-generator.ts:144`). **No upstream file is patched to include own code** - the VS Code pair "own layer + entry-module graft" collapses into a JSON key (`10`, "The short version"). The constant graft set of a Theia product may be empty. @status:spec/done

The layer `entry-module` is not provided: an artifact of that layer in a `theia` patch set is refused by `verify` with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, and the ladder of `ck-intervene` skips the rung. @status:spec/done

A Theia extension is own code (a workspace package), not a VS Code-style built-in extension; the `own-extensions` layer is therefore not provided in the first version. VS Code extensions run in Theia as plugins (`.vsix` under `theiaPluginsDir`, `theiaPlugins` in the application manifest) - a later capability `own-plugins` may materialize a product's plugins from the delta (`06-extension-model.md`, the two mechanisms). @status:spec/done
3. service-override: rebind plus dependency order

A service override is `rebind(Id).to(Impl)` (or `.toService`/`.toDynamicValue`) inside the own package's `ContainerModule`; it wins because `ExtensionPackageCollector` pushes a package after its dependencies, so the own module loads after the module it overrides (`04-dependency-injection.md`; `extension-package-collector.ts:76-84`). @status:spec/done

The verifier of a `service-override` record checks two things: the `rebind` call of the declared service identifier in the declared own module, and the dependency edge from the own package to the package that binds the service (a `rebind` without the edge may load first and be overridden itself). There is no `registerSingleton` call site and no forbidden-service list from upstream; `forbiddenServiceIds` starts empty and grows from measurement. @status:spec/done

Open question of the spike (`open-questions.md` 4): whether a `rebind` in a child container behaves like one in the root container for the overrides a product wants. Until measured, the verifier accepts only root-container modules and names the limitation. The limitation is implemented (a module that does not default-export a `ContainerModule` is refused, and the engine counts only a bare `rebind(Id)` call, so a `child.rebind(...)` never satisfies an override); **the question itself is still open** - P5 did not run a Theia application and could not measure it. @status:spec/done
theia PROP-004: Build, watch, lint, test, packaging

Dependencies: `npm ci` on Node ≥ 24 with Python 3.13 available for native modules; install runs `node-gyp install`, `theia-patch`, `compute-references` and `lerna run afterInstall` (`03-build-watch-lint-test.md`; `package.json:94-95`). The CI profile's dependency step is `npm ci`; the tree must be byte-identical after it (upstream's own clean-tree gate, `08`). @status:spec/done

**One install, one dependency root: `node_modules/` of the tree root.** This monorepo is a single npm workspace and every package of it, the build tooling included, is hoisted into that one directory; the root of this upstream carries `configs/`, `dev-packages/`, `examples/`, `packages/` and `scripts/` and **no `build/` directory at all** (`02-repository-layout.md`). Measured by the first real consumer of this type on a real clone: the engine used to demand the npm receipt of a second root, `build/node_modules/.package-lock.json`, as a module constant taken from the first family, so `ci --profile build` could not go green over any tree of this family at any state - and it refused with «provide node_modules» over a tree whose `node_modules/` was there. The roots are now the type's answer (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS`) and this type answers exactly one. @status:impl/done

Compile: `lerna run compile` (per package `theiaext compile` = `tsc --project .`) for the whole tree, or `lerna run compile --scope <own package>` for own code; the application bundle is `theia build` in the application directory (esbuild since 1.75.0; webpack is gone - `bundler-generator.ts:43-45`). **Measured in P5**: the contract has no slot for a one-shot compile - the engine compiles through the watch channels and packages through `packageBuild` - so `lerna run compile --scope` is a command of the protocol and of a person, not an answer of the type; both were measured on a real clone in P5: `npm ci` 46 s on the pristine tree, `npm run compile` of the whole tree 68 s over 92 projects, and the own package alone 2 s afterwards. Two facts came out of that measurement and belong to the type's protocol rather than to its answers: **the own package has to be compiled after the tree**, because the compile of a package needs the `lib/` of every package it depends on, and **`npm ci` refuses once the own package exists** (`Missing: <own package> from lock file`), because a workspace member is part of the lockfile - a fork regenerates `package-lock.json` with `npm install` once, carries the result as the tree's own, and `npm ci` is green again from then on. @status:spec/done

`build up` starts two channels: `typecheck-watch` = `tsc -b -w` at the tree root (project references), `bundle-watch` = `theia build --watch` in the application directory; `build errors` reads their logs; foreign-watcher markers are those two command lines (`03`, watchers). **Both of them are this type's `build.defaultChannels`** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-BUILD-CHANNELS`), measured by the first real consumer: while the default was a module constant naming the channels of the first family, only `typecheck` matched and `ci --profile build` never bundled the application of this one - a build profile that did not build. @status:spec/done

Lint: `lerna run lint --scope <own package>` (`theiaext lint`, type-aware eslint per package) for the own directory and `npm run lint` for the full tree; the full run is the gate of a phase that adds a package, as `CONF-OWN-EXTENSION-PASSES-THE-FULL-LINT` says for the same reason. **Measured on a real clone in P5 and corrected here**: `lerna run <script> --scope <own package>` cannot reach the own package of a codkit patch set at all - the tool excludes the own root through `.git/info/exclude`, lerna discovers its packages with the git ignores applied, and the run ends in `EFILTER No packages remain after filtering`. The type therefore runs the scripts of the own package by workspace, `npm run lint --workspace <ownRoot>`, which reads the workspace globs of the manifest and finds the package whatever git thinks of it; the full-tree `npm run lint` is upstream's own command and covers every package except that one, which is why the own package is linted first and separately. The same holds for the tests (`THEIA-TEST-RUNNERS`) and for a one-shot compile. @status:spec/done

Three runners (`12-app-test-harness.md`): unit tests `theiaext test` (nyc + mocha over `lib/**/*.spec.js`, selected per package by `lerna run test --scope`); in-page tests `theia test . --test-spec=<glob>` (mocha inside the running frontend with the live container); system tests with `@theia/playwright`. The own-root glob of the CI profile is the package scope, not a path glob. **Implemented in P5**: the contract has one slot for the tests of the own root, and it carries the first runner - `lerna run test --scope <own package>`; the in-page runner and the Playwright suite are a step of the protocol, outside `ci`, exactly as the browser suites of the first type are. The selection is `npm run test --workspace <ownRoot>` for the reason `THEIA-LINT` measured; on a real clone the generated skeleton compiled in 2 s, linted clean in 2 s and its spec passed under nyc with 100% coverage of the two files. @status:spec/done

Upstream packages no desktop application: no electron-builder configuration, no signing, no installer, no `.icns`/`.ico` generation; its release artefact is npm packages, and its contract with a packager is the built `lib/` of the application (`11-release-packaging.md`). The type's package build is therefore `theia build` of the application; the installer is a product artifact (the product declares its packager and its config in its own delta), and the type's `ci --profile build` ends at the built application unless the product declares more. **Implemented after the first real consumer:** «unless the product declares more» had no field to be declared in - the package build was always exactly `theia build` - so `ci --profile build` could never reach the product's own installer. `typeConfig.packageScript` (optional, an npm script of the application's manifest) is that field. **Amended when the packaging verb arrived:** the two halves are two answers, not one list - `build.packageBuild` stays `theia build` of the application whatever the product declares, and `build.packageDistributable` is `npm run <packageScript> --workspace <applicationRoot>` when the field is set and empty when it is not (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`). They are separate so that `codkit package --skip-type-build` can run only the product's half over a tree the watch channels already built. The type still names no packager: which one the script runs, and what configures it, live in the product's delta. @status:spec/done

**The package build of this family compiles before it bundles, and the reason is that the bundler does not complain when it should.** `build.packageBuild` is three commands in this order: `npm run compile` at the tree root (`tsc -b` over the project references - incremental, so it costs seconds on a warm tree and the full 68 s of ##THEIA-COMPILE only on a cold one), then `npm run compile --workspace <ownRoot>` (the own package can only be compiled once the packages it depends on have their `lib/`, ##THEIA-COMPILE), then `theia build` in the application. It used to be the bundle alone, and that was wrong in exactly the case the tool creates for itself: `codkit load --fresh` removes the build outputs its cleanup whitelist names, `**/lib/` among them, so the tree a packaging run starts from is uncompiled. esbuild then **does not fail** over the missing `<ownPackage>/lib/…` - it leaves the import as a runtime require and reports a pass with zero errors - and the run ends green with a package that builds, starts, and carries not one line of the product's own code. Measured on 2026-09-09 on the first packaging of a real fork of this family. The engine is unchanged: the order of the commands is an answer of the type, and `codkit package --skip-type-build` still skips all three, because a tree the watch channels already built is exactly the case where none of them is needed. @status:impl/done

**This family leaves no packaging residue**: neither half writes into a tracked file of the tree - the build of the application writes its own `lib/` and `src-gen/`, and a packager the product declares writes the application's `dist/` - so `build.packageScratch` is empty and `codkit package` has nothing to put back beyond the overlay targets it materialized itself (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`). Unlike the first family, whose bundler rewrites the manifest of every add-on it packages (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#VSCODE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`), nothing here edits the sources in passing. @status:impl/done

**Both halves write inside the managed tree, so this type can name where the artifact lands.** `build.packageOutputs` is `<applicationRoot>/dist/` - the directory a packager of this family leaves its result in (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-002#THEIA-PACKAGER-OUTPUT`, which already counts it as a build output of the application) - and `codkit package` prints it when it exists. Unlike the first family, nothing here is written beside the tree, so nothing has to be reported as unnameable (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#VSCODE-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS`). @status:spec/done

Nothing is stamped at build time - no sha, no date, no quality channel (`09-build-time-stamps.md`); what is baked into `src-gen/` is the frontend and backend configuration, the page title and the extension inventory. A product that wants a commit in its About dialog adds it through its own package (a generated constant written by `load` from the pin), not through the type. @status:spec/done
